sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: minor-supply suspensions, aggressive driving tiers, under-21 versus adult limits, the open container boundary, seizure reporting and revocation
Look-alike penalties, limits and duties from the impairment, aggressive driving, medical and revocation pages, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec18-R01 | anchor: A01
Supplying liquor to a minor can cost up to 30 days of license suspension on a first conviction and up to six months on a second or later one. [A01]
Why it matters: group minor supply; difficulty three; confusable sec18-F13 versus sec18-F14.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-R02 | anchor: A01
An unlocked compartment within reach counts as part of the passenger compartment, while the trunk, or the space behind the last upright seat when there is no trunk, does not. [A01]
Why it matters: group open container; difficulty three; confusable sec18-F10 versus sec18-F11.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-R03 | anchor: A01
The open container exemption covers only passengers in a bus, limousine, taxi or motor home living area, so it never covers the driver. [A01]
Why it matters: group open container; difficulty two; prereq sec18-F09.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-R04 | anchor: A01
Over-the-counter allergy and cold medicines can impair driving just as prescription drugs can, so the label check applies to both. [A01]
Why it matters: group medications; difficulty two; prereq sec18-F04.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec18-R05 | anchor: A02
A first aggressive driving offense means Traffic Survival School and a possible 30-day suspension, while a second within 24 months is a Class 1 misdemeanor with a 12-month suspension. [A02]
Why it matters: group aggressive driving; difficulty three; confusable sec18-F25 versus sec18-F26.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-R06 | anchor: A02
Aggressive driving needs speeding plus two of the listed violations, not speeding alone or a single violation. [A02]
Why it matters: group aggressive driving; difficulty three; prereq sec18-F23.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-R07 | anchor: A02
Under 21, any impairing trace of alcohol or drugs brings a 2-year suspension, while for any driver staying below 0.08 BAC still allows a DUI arrest. [A02]
Why it matters: group impairment limits; difficulty three; confusable sec18-F20 versus sec18-F21.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-R08 | anchor: A02
Survey data puts the ages most likely to drive after drinking at 21 to 29. [A02]
Why it matters: group ages; difficulty two; prereq sec18-F17.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec18-R09 | anchor: A03
A seizure within 90 days before applying must be reported, while an already licensed driver who has a seizure must stop driving, notify MVD and get a medical exam. [A03]
Why it matters: group medical reporting; difficulty three; confusable sec18-F35 versus sec18-F36.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-R10 | anchor: A03
When a revocation period ends, the privilege stays revoked until an investigation clears it, and reinstating costs the application fee plus a $20 reinstatement fee. [A03]
Why it matters: group revocation; difficulty three; confusable sec18-F48 versus sec18-F49.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec18-R11 | anchor: A03
Fresh air, music, gum and frequent stops help fight drowsiness, but rest is the only safe remedy. [A03]
Why it matters: group fatigue; difficulty two; confusable sec18-F45 versus sec18-F41.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]
